issues.failure_explanation: By the paper's own convention, Λ_t(y,x) is the rate of jumping from state x to state y (the column-sum-zero condition confirms this: Σ_y Λ_t(y,x)=0 for each x). The loss integrand should weight each candidate jump target y by the forward rate from the current state x_t to y, i.e. Λ_t(y, x_t). The source instead uses Λ_t(x_t, y), which is the rate from y to x_t. For asymmetric rate matrices (e.g. the masked rate matrix discussed in the same section) the two entries differ, so the displayed loss is not the correct score-matching objective.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \gL^{h, \lambda} f = h^{-1} \gL(h f) - h^{-1} f \gL h = \gL f + h^{-1} \Gamma(h, f)
\Gamma_t^*(p_t, f) := \gL_t^*(p_t f) - p_t \gL_t^* f - f \gL_t^* p_t

issues.failure_explanation: The standard carré du champ is Γ_std(h,f) = gL(hf) − h gL f − f gL h, and the identity gL^{h,λ}f = gL f + h⁻¹Γ_std(h,f) follows by direct expansion. The paper instead defines Γ(h,f) = h gL(h⁻¹f) − f gL h⁻¹. For gL = ½d²/dx², h(x)=x, f(x)=x: the left side h⁻¹gL(hf)−h⁻¹f gL h = 1/x, while gL f + h⁻¹Γ_paper(h,f) = 0 + (1/x)(−1/x²) = −1/x³. The displayed identity is therefore false with the paper's Γ. The paper also uses the standard definition Γ_t^*(p_t,f) = gL_t^*(p_t f) − p_t gL_t^* f − f gL_t^* p_t in the time-reversal theorem, making the two definitions inconsistent within the same paper. The main Radon–Nikodym derivative formula in thm:doob is correct and independent of this Γ definition.

issues.title: Doob h-transform theorem uses a non-standard carré du champ making the conservative-case identity false
issues.why_classification: The correction is a local redefinition of one auxiliary quantity in a supporting clause of a theorem whose main statement (the RN derivative) is already correct. No downstream result depends on the erroneous identity, and the fix requires no new construction or argument.

issues.failure_explanation: Two defects are present. First, the score-ratio identity above uses ŝ_t (time t), but the reuse formula in the denominator uses ŝ_{T-t} (time T−t); these are different functions unless φ_t = φ_{T-t}. Second, even after correcting the time index, the claimed equality is false in general: J[Āλ^φ_t(·,x)] = φ_t(x)^{-1}∫φ_t(y)λ(y−x)dy depends on x through the shifted Lévy kernel λ(y−x), while the RHS evaluates the integral at the fixed reference point y^{ref}. The two integrals ∫φ_t(y)λ(y−x)dy and ∫φ_t(y)λ(y−y^{ref})dy are equal only if φ_t is constant or λ is a pure mass (not a Gaussian kernel). The formula therefore does not hold for the Gaussian Lévy measure used in the experiment.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Remove or correct the reuse identity. A valid approach is to evaluate J[Āλ^φ_t(·,x)] = φ_t(x)^{-1}∫φ_t(y)λ(y−x)dy independently for each sample x (e.g. by the FFT-based quadrature the paper already describes), or to state explicit conditions (e.g. φ_t approximately constant on the support of λ) under which the reuse is a controlled approximation rather than an exact equality.
issues.overall_effect: The stated computational shortcut for evaluating the jump intensity integral in the backward simulation is not valid. A practitioner following the formula would obtain incorrect Poisson means for jump counts, leading to biased backward trajectories. The theoretical guarantees (thm:numerical_error, cor:error_bound) are unaffected because they bound the exact backward process, not this approximate computation.
issues.title: Jump-model integral-reuse formula is algebraically incorrect and has a time-index inconsistency
issues.why_classification: The formula is a practical computational suggestion in the experiments section, not a theorem or a step in any proof. The theoretical error bounds and score-matching losses are derived from the exact generators and are unaffected. The repair is to delete or qualify a single displayed identity; no architectural change to the framework is required.
